claims.text: The initial material is a conventionally composed high-entropy alloy produced by standard casting and homogenization with an equiaxed microstructure.
A controlled minor zirconium addition can be introduced into the high-entropy alloy formulation.
A minor zirconium addition will promote in situ formation of nanoscale Zr-rich precipitates.
The Zr-rich nanoscale precipitates will be thermally stable at elevated temperature.
The Zr-rich precipitates will be distributed both at grain boundaries and within grains.
The Zr-rich precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The Zr-rich precipitates will restrict grain-boundary sliding.
Obstructing dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will delay creep onset.
The zirconium-added alloy will have a lower elevated-temperature creep strain rate than an otherwise identically processed zirconium-free baseline alloy.
The zirconium-added alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than an otherwise identically processed zirconium-free baseline alloy.
The proposed improvement should hold during high-temperature mechanical loading around 800 °C where creep is a primary concern.
The magnitude of improvement depends on optimization of zirconium content and processing parameters.
